No, it does not use a database transaction. According to [[write-journal]], the rollback mechanism "provides all-or-nothing semantics for writes without needing a database transaction — the journal itself acts as the transaction log, held in process memory for the duration of a single run."

The journal is an in-memory data structure that records prior file state before any write occurs, and on failure it can roll back writes by restoring previous content or deleting newly created files. It achieves transactional semantics purely through this journaling approach rather than relying on a database.
